answer: Quadratic staking erosion forces validators to lock collateral C with slashing penalty λ·C², creating a cost surface. Marginal attack cost for a Sybil cluster of size k scales as k^{1+α} (α>0) since each new identity must post collateral and suffer slashing, yielding super‑linear capital expenditure. When total stake surpasses the security threshold Θ = V·(1+δ) where V is maximal extractable value and δ a safety margin, expected attack utility turns negative, establishing a robust Nash equilibrium across the copper ridge bridge of consensus.
